content.content:
A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

    ask:
        Ask is for simply asking a question. A question runs straight away,
        separately from any Code, Chain, or Spec task, even while the harness
        is working on one. Any number of questions can be asked, and they all
        run at the same time; asking another never stops or waits for one
        already running.

        Each question's progress and results are shown in a task table, as in
        the @{MessageList}. The questions stack directly above the tabs, the
        newest nearest them, over the bottom of the message list rather than
        pushing it up, and each slides up out of the chat input with an
        animation as it is asked. While the harness works on a question, it is
        a single row showing the latest thing the harness did. A finished
        question is a row with its status and first line.

        Once a question is complete, it opens onto a heading, with its status
        and first line, above its full task table, which scrolls once it gets
        tall, with a @{ScrollColumnScope} and its lock to the bottom. Only one question is open at a time: opening another closes the
        one open back down to its row. Clicking an open question's heading
        closes it down to its row, and clicking a finished question's row opens
        it again. Each question has a close button, which removes it and stops
        it if it is still running, leaving the others running. A closed
        question becomes a previous answer.

    previousAnswers:
        Previous answers are a @{HistoryListScope}, shown only while the Ask
        tab is selected, at the top of the questions stacked above the tabs.
        It lists every question asked before and closed: those saved with the
        project and those closed since. Its row reads "No previous answers",
        "1 previous answer", or "N previous answers", and while expanded,
        "Back to the questions". Expanded, the list slides up out of the chat
        input, as questions do, above any questions still open. The questions
        asked from now on carry on the conversation the latest of them left
        off.

    escape:
        Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat
        input.

content.text:
The answer drawer now opens to 80% of the space above the chat input, and you can resize it by dragging its top edge. The drawer means the questions area above the chat input, whether a question is open or the previous answers are showing. I haven't tried it in the running app.

- **Opening:** whatever is open grows to fill that 80%, after the drawer's other rows, instead of stopping at the old fixed heights (400px for a question, 360px for previous answers). It still slides up as it opens.
- **Short answers:** a short answer also opens to the full 80%, leaving empty space below it.
- **Resizing:** hovering the top edge shows a resize cursor and a thin highlight line. Dragging follows the pointer directly, without the slide, and stays between 20% and 95% of the space.
- **Keeping the size:** the dragged size carries over to the next question or list you open, until the app quits. It isn't saved between launches.
- **Both open:** if a question and the previous answers are open together, they split the space.

**Test:** a new test checks that an open question fills 80%, and that dragging the edge to halfway makes it 50%. It also checks that opening another question keeps 50%. The previous answers list isn't covered by a test. The suite shows 125 passed, 1 skipped (it needs the real harness), and the same palette test failing as before. The build has no warnings.

**Spec:** `ChatInputScope` has a new `answerDrawer` section, and the ask section now says an open question's table fills the drawer. `piton check` and `piton build check` pass. The code is in `src/prompt_mode.rs`.
